source.title: The Possibility of Real-Time and Long-Term Predictions for Geomagnetic Storms Using Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: The study varies training epochs and reports prediction accuracy, bearing on the epoch-wise version, but does not test the double-descent curve as a whole.
record.gate_note: Only the epoch-variation results for predictions of September 1999 and October 2003 bear on a claim version. The study does not vary model size or sample size, and does not test an effective-complexity account, noise or regularization dependence, or complexity counting. No relevant result values are extractable from the cited figures beyond the qualitative comparison stated in the text.
record.test_reason: An applied geomagnetic-storm forecasting paper with fixed-size BPNNs (two hidden layers of 10 neurons). It compares 2000 vs 2500 epochs only to choose a training length; no sweep can show fall-rise-fall. Belkin et al. is cited only for the bias-variance tradeoff. Model size, interpolation, label noise and regularization are never varied. It neither tests nor uses double descent.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that both BPNN models are stable for real-time and long-term Dst prediction. They judge 2000 epochs an appropriate tradeoff, since 2500 epochs gave only slightly better accuracy at extra computing cost.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies training duration in fixed-size BPNNs for geomagnetic prediction; it does not reproduce a double-descent experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction accuracy was reported as slightly better at 2500 epochs than at 2000; the epoch comparison is limited to these settings in the text.
record.problems: For the epoch-wise claim, only a qualitative comparison of 2000 and 2500 epochs is stated; the relevant figures provide no extractable numeric values in the text, and this limited comparison cannot establish the curve shape.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results left out.

untested.parts: All: model size is never varied.
All: only two epoch settings, used for selection.
All: training-period length is varied (Fig. 15, longer is better), but far from any interpolation threshold.
All: initial-weight ranges are varied, but not noise or regularization.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' should be 'cites_only/T6'. Belkin et al. (2019) appears only in a citation list about overfitting and the bias-variance tradeoff. Training-length variation (Fig. 15) shows more data reducing error in a heavily under-parameterized regime; this does not bear on V3.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise test error across model sizes and the interpolation threshold.
The study compares 2000 and 2500 epochs but does not establish a fall-rise-fall curve or locate a peak across a broad training-time sweep.
Test error as training-sample size increases near interpolation.
Double descent across model classes or capacity beyond interpolation.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across axes.
The role of label noise or variance, multiple peaks, and optimally tuned regularization.
Whether effective parameter counting turns second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
